description: The bar chart illustrates the annual number of hateful communication datasets published from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the geographic location of the researchers who created them, as presented in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets.” The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. Each year features a grouped set of vertical bars, each color-coded to represent a different researcher location: blue for “Other,” orange for “USA,” green for “IN” (India), red for “UK,” purple for “IT” (Italy), and brown for “DE” (Germany). The chart shows a general upward trend in dataset production over time, with a notable surge between 2017 and 2020. In 2019, the “Other” category (blue) reaches its peak at approximately 100 datasets, followed closely by “USA” (orange) at around 80. In 2020, “USA” and “Other” remain dominant, while “IN” and “UK” also show strong contributions. By 2022, dataset counts decline across most categories, with “Other” and “USA” still leading but at lower levels (~30–40). The “Other” category consistently contributes the most datasets in most years, followed by “USA,” while “IN,” “UK,” “IT,” and “DE” show more variable and generally lower contributions. The chart visually emphasizes the growing volume of research activity in this domain, particularly from researchers outside the explicitly named countries and from the USA.
